findings.title: Phone (390×844): the desk view crops off SEND and the RADIO/MICRO keys, and touch has no other way to send, so the job can't be finished
findings.problem: At 390×844 the bench camera can't fit the 4.4 m desk. In the bench shot the band row starts at 'RMAL' (THERMAL): the RADIO and MICRO keys are past the left edge. On the right, the power keys are cut at '100 m' and the green SEND cap (table x +1.95) is entirely off-screen. In bench mode the walking controls hide (ui.css:246). There is no HTML touch fallback for band, power, hatch or send, and a phone has no keyboard for 1–5 or Enter. A touch player therefore can't pick Radio, which Delivery 1 needs, and can't press SEND at all, so the job can't be completed on a phone. The phone layout also moves the station toast to just under the panel (ui.css:255), where it covers the top of the hall map, the surface the player drags to aim. The phone joystick and the action buttons show the game is meant to be played by touch, so this blocks play there. (R3B M1 already noted 'Phone bench layout OPEN'; this is the concrete spectrum consequence.)
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-play-92-phone-bench.jpg (SEND off the right edge; RADIO/MICRO off the left; toast over the map)
src/game.ts:372 (bench distance = view.distance × clamp(1.25/aspect, 1, 2.1): capped at 2.1, so portrait can't widen enough)
src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:59 (view distance 6.1), :140-141 (SEND at table x+1.95), :118 (band keys from x −2.01)
findings.fix:
Pick one of two fixes:
(a) Add a per-station portrait view. Station gets an optional `portraitView:{distance,pitch,lookY}`. For spectrum use about {distance:6.1, pitch:1.25, lookY:.42} and raise the game.ts:372 clamp cap from 2.1 to about 3.0 when `cam.aspect<.6`, so the whole 4.5 m table fits.
(b) Better for touch: under `body[data-bench]` with `(pointer:coarse)`, render a compact HTML control strip from the station's clickables: five band chips, 1/10/100 mW, HATCH and a big SEND. Hide the 3D labels' reliance.
Also move the phone toast below the map (top: calc(84px + 30vh + map height)), or show it as a one-line chip at the bottom.
findings.verify: Launch spectrum at {width:390,height:844}, reach the desk, and take a bench shot: RADIO and SEND are fully on screen. Script a touch-only run (page.touchscreen.tap on the on-screen controls, no keyboard) through all three deliveries to snap().won===true.
findings.verify_reason:
I reproduced this at 390×844. In the bench shot the band row starts at 'RMAL', so RADIO and MICRO are off the left edge, and the power keys are cut at '100' with SEND entirely off the right edge. I scanned the canvas for pointer-cursor hits: the right-most clickable is at x=386, and tapping there only set power to 100. The only visible HTML button at the bench is 'Pause'. The prompt pill (objectives.ts:93) has no tap handler. At the bench, .hud .actions and .stick are hidden (ui.css:246), and orbit needs a right button (game.ts:172), so a touch player can't pan. Delivery 1 needs Radio, and every delivery needs SEND, so a touch-only player can't finish. The phone toast rule (ui.css:255, top: 84px+30vh) puts it over the hall map (reviewer shot 92). | P0 re-check confirmed: I couldn't refute it for a portrait phone. I could only narrow it: landscape is a workaround, but nothing tells the player about it.

PORTRAIT 390×844: reproduced. Shot mockups/review5/shots/p0check-spectrum-play-portrait-bench.jpg shows the band row starting at 'RMAL', so RADIO and MICRO are off the left edge. The power keys are cut at '100' and there is no SEND anywhere on screen. In my earlier a.mjs probe, the hover-cursor scan found no clickable past the screen edge. At the bench, src/game.ts:172 sends touch (button 0) to benchPointer, and orbit only listens for button 2, so a touch player can't swing the view. src/ui/ui.css:246 hides .actions and .stick at the bench. The only HTML controls left are Pause and the Esc 'Stand up' chip (src/ui/objectives.ts:96). The bench yaw is forced to face the stand (src/game.ts:372), so standing up and coming back at another angle doesn't help either. The code means portrait to be supported: game.ts:371 says 'Portrait screens are narrow: pull back so the width of the table still fits', and nothing in src asks the player to rotate (no orientation or landscape hint). So on the phone's natural orientation a touch player can't pick Radio, which Delivery 1 needs, and can't SEND at all. The room can't be finished.

LANDSCAPE 844×390, with hasTouch, isMobile and (pointer:coarse) true: a touch player can finish it. Script: mockups/review5/tools/p0check-spectrum-play/b.mjs and c.mjs. A real page.touchscreen.tap test found every control:
- band keys at (191..301, 251)
- power keys at (572 and 602, 236)
- hatch at (547, 263)
- SEND at about (650, 243)

The tap at (191, 251) set band to radio. The tap at (650, 243) then delivered {job:'store', tier:3, margin:11} with 0 mistakes; see shot p0check-spectrum-play-12-land-radio-send-by-touch.jpg. But in landscape, .station-panel (ui.css:218, pointer-events:none) covers the power keys, hatch and SEND completely; see shots p0check-spectrum-play-10-land-bench-d1.jpg and p0check-spectrum-play-landscape-big-bench.jpg. Taps pass through the panel to the canvas, so the player has to tap a control they can't see. My first scan logged 3 'mistakes' from blind taps on that hidden area (tap 650,243 / 637,250 / 664,253 while the band was wrong). That's a serious P1 in its own right: the panel hides the controls at the 700–1000 px widths above the max-width:700 phone rule.

Verdict: keep P0, scoped to portrait phones. It blocks the job on the intended orientation, and the landscape workaround is invisible: you'd have to rotate the phone and tap under an opaque panel. I agree with the earlier correction that fix (b) is better: an HTML control strip under body[data-bench] with (pointer:coarse), giving band chips, 1/10/100 mW, HATCH and a big SEND. A cheap stopgap is to make .prompt-pill tappable. Also, in landscape bench mode, shrink or move .station-panel so it stops covering the right third of the desk (power, hatch, SEND).

To verify: a hasTouch run at 390×844 and at 844×390, using only touchscreen.tap, through all three deliveries until snapshot().won===true. Retake the bench shots and check that SEND and RADIO are visible and not covered.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-spectrum-play-32-phone-bench.jpg (RADIO/MICRO cut on the left, SEND absent on the right)
v3.mjs log: clickable max x 386; right-edge taps changed power 1→100 only; HTML buttons at bench: ['Pause']
src/ui/objectives.ts:93 (prompt pill has no listener; only the bench chip at :96 does)
src/game.ts:172 (bench pointerdown routes button 0 to benchPointer; orbit is button 2 only)
findings.fix_correction: Prefer fix (b), the HTML control strip under body[data-bench] with (pointer:coarse). Fix (a) has a problem: raising the game.ts:372 cap to 3.0 at aspect 0.46 makes the 4.4 m desk only about 390 px wide. The band keys (0.17 m) would then be about 15 px across, far below a 44 px touch target, so (a) alone leaves the controls hard to hit. A cheap extra fallback: make .prompt-pill tappable (pointerdown → the same action as its key, so 'Enter · Send' sends). Verify: a touchscreen-only Playwright run (page.touchscreen.tap, no keyboard) through all three deliveries reaches won===true.

findings.title: From the game camera the storeroom and lab pads, the pod and Pip are hidden behind the 2.1 m brick wall and the 2.05 m shutter
findings.problem:
Steps 1, 4 and 6 all end with 'set the pod on the pad', but two of the three pads can't be seen from the default camera.
- **Storeroom:** with Pip inside carrying the pod (shot 09) or after setting it down (shot 10), only Pip's hard hat shows above the brick front wall. The pad, the pod and Pip's body are all hidden. Only the bouncing marker floats above the shelf.
- **Lab:** the same happens behind the metal shutter (shots 22, 23). Pip is a hat behind the roller box, and the 'GLASS LAB PAD' tag and the pod are invisible.
- **Why:** the occlusion fade casts one ray to p.y+0.4 (≈1.17 m). At the station zoom (≈18.5, pitch ≈0.52 rad), that ray passes the wall about 2.4 m in front of Pip at ≈2.5 m height, above the 2.1 m brick and the 2.05 m shutter. So the wall never fades even though it covers Pip's legs, the held pod and the floor pad.
- **Inconsistent:** a step closer to the wall the ray does hit, and the bricks fade (shot 60). The player sees the wall sometimes fade and sometimes not.
- **At close zoom:** at zoom 9 the shutter fades correctly (shot 24), so the content is fine; the occlusion test is the bug.

A new player can't see whether the pod landed on the ring, so they rely on the sound and the card ticking. This breaks the 'camera never hides Pip' and 'target never hidden' rules.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-play-60-store-orbit-0.jpg (same wall does fade when the ray happens to hit it)
findings.fix:
Pick one, or combine:
1. In src/game.ts:387, cast three rays (to p.y−0.6 for the feet, p.y+0.2 and p.y+0.9), plus one to the held item's position. Fade any occluder hit by any of them, down to opacity ≤0.25 (the rulebook value; today 0.15 is fine).
2. For this room, add a 'cutaway when inside' rule in station.update(): when Pip's z is less than STORE.z1 (or LAB.z1) and Pip is inside the room's x-range, force those slabs' materials to opacity 0.25, or scale them to a 0.9 m stub like the shell walls (game.ts:384-385).
3. Also put a short vertical beacon (a glow ring, or a 1.5 m translucent pillar in the pad colour) on the current pad, so it reads over the wall.
findings.verify: Take shots 09, 10, 22 and 23 again at the default zoom. Pip's whole body, the pod and the pad ring are visible, with the brick or shutter faded. Then sweep 8 yaws (g.orbit(±200)) with Pip on each pad: at least 70% of Pip's pixels stay visible in every frame.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced this at the default station zoom. With the pod on the storeroom pad, only Pip's hard hat shows above an opaque brick wall, and the pad and pod are hidden (shot 04). On the glass lab pad, Pip, the pod and the pad are all hidden behind the opaque shutter (shot 10). In shot 03, a moment earlier while Pip was still carrying the pod, the wall is partly faded, so the fade does come and go as described. The code matches: one ray to p.y+.4 (game.ts:387), and the room walls are fading occluders. The card and prompt at that moment also don't help (see #5).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-spectrum-play-10-pod-on-lab-pad.jpg (shutter opaque; Pip, pod and pad hidden)

findings.title: A successful delivery is never seen: at the desk the beam, pulse and pad burst are hidden, and the desk flips to the next job within a frame
findings.problem:
The payoff of each delivery (the message flying through brick, bouncing off the mirror, slipping through the hatch) happens where the player can't see it.
- **In the room:** at the desk the room beam and floor marks are hidden (station.ts:374, :390) and the pulse is hidden while atBench (:397). The confetti for an at-bench send is a small burst behind the desk (shared.ts cheer), and the pad star burst only fires when not at the bench (:235).
- **On the desk:** SEND immediately does jobIndex++ and re-aims the tower at the next pad (:236). So 0.3 s after a success the hall map already shows the next delivery's failure: in shot 15 the map shows a red X on the lab shutter, and the LINK screen says 'POD NOT ON THE PAD', while the only sign of success is the toast '“STOCK CHECK AT 4” · Elegant (11 dB)'.
- **Coworkers:** the storeroom keeper and the lab scientist never visibly react to receiving their message.

The result: three anticlimactic toasts. This is the Good Job 'juice' moment, and it is missing.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-play-15-bench-radio-delivered.jpg (0.3 s after success: next job's blocked state already drawn)
src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:233-236 (jobIndex++ and the aim reset on the same frame)
findings.fix:
1. Add a 'delivered' hold of about 1.6 s to station.ts act('send'). Keep the current job's route on the map, and animate the pulse along the map path on the hall-map canvas (drawMap: a bright dot moving along drawnPath at 9 m/s, scaled). Flash the destination pad on the map green, and only then advance jobIndex and re-aim.
2. During the hold, show the room as well. Either cut to a 1.2 s 'delivery cam' looking at the pad (reuse the win push-in code in game.ts:373 with the target set to PADS[j.pad]), or show a picture-in-picture of the pad. In that shot the receiving coworker cheers (set npc.alarm-style cheer, or a happy hop for 1 s) and the pod lamp blinks.
3. Play a distinct 'message received' chime from the pad position.
findings.verify: Take a shot at +0.3, +0.8 and +1.5 s after a successful SEND at the desk. The delivered route and a pulse are visible on the map (or the pad is in view), the pad flashes, and the next job's state appears only after the hold.
findings.verify_reason: I took a shot 0.3 s after a successful Radio SEND at the desk. The map already shows the next job's red X on the lab shutter, LINK reads 'POD NOT ON THE PAD', the panel reads 'Into the shuttered lab · blocked: metal shutter', and the card has moved to step 4. The only success cue is the toast '“STOCK CHECK AT 4” · Elegant (11 dB)'. The code matches: jobIndex++ and the re-aim at station.ts:236 run in the same act() call; the beam and pulse are hidden at the bench (:374, :390, :397); and the pad star burst only fires when !atBench (:235).
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log 'after send': pill 'E Fetch the pod', station.job 1, reading.blocked 'metal', podOk false
findings.fix_correction: The fix is sound. Two side effects need handling. (1) tests/station-spectrum.spec.ts checks s.job===1 straight after send (second test), so the hold needs those assertions to wait about 1.7 s, or the hold should be skipped under ?manual. (2) During the hold, E/Esc and the band keys must either act on the next job or be ignored explicitly, so a fast player can't send twice to the same pad.

findings.title: The win push-in shows Pip at the desk with no beam, and the 'rainbow lights up' finale is out of frame
findings.problem:
At the win the camera pushes in on the desk (winFocus = table, game.ts:398). Pip is in frame, which is good, but the machine that 'came alive' (the tower's beam through the smoke and mesh into the quiet room) isn't drawn.
- **No beam:** station.update() sets beam.visible=!atBench (station.ts:374/390), and after win() the game stops stepping (game.ts:457 only steps while !won). The leaveBench() in win (game.ts:353) therefore never gets a station update, and the beam stays hidden. In shot 44 the turret points right and no thermal beam leaves it.
- **No finale:** lightUp() glows the floor rainbow stripes at z 6.2–6.9 (room.ts:148), which are below or behind the push-in camera and don't appear in shots 44 or 45.
- **No destination:** the quiet room, where the last message landed, is off-frame to the right.

The final beat is Pip waving at an unchanged desk.
findings.fix:
1. In game.win(), after leaveBench(), call this.station.update?.(0) once, or add a Station.onWin() that spectrum implements as `this.beam.visible=true; this.drawBeam(this.reading())` with the last delivered route kept, not the 'next job' route.
2. Give the station a `winFocus()` override. For spectrum, use the midpoint between TX and the last pad (about (3.9,1.5,3.5)) with distance about 10, so the tower, the beam, the smoke and the quiet room are all in frame.
3. Also light the three destination pad rings and the tower beacon in lightUp, rather than (or as well as) the floor stripes behind the camera.
findings.verify: Take shots at +0.4 and +1.8 s after the last SEND. The thermal beam runs from the tower through the smoke into the quiet room, Pip and the tower sit inside the centre 70% of the frame, and the lit pads are visible.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the win at 0.4 s and 1.8 s after the last SEND. The turret points toward the quiet room but draws no thermal beam, and the quiet room is out of frame; Pip and the desk fill the frame. The cause: game.win() calls leaveBench() (game.ts:353), but frame() only steps while !won (game.ts:457), so station.update() never runs again and the beam keeps beam.visible=false from the bench. win() does set this.beam.visible=true, but that is the decor beam (game.ts:117 via decorate), not SpectrumDesk.beam.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:117 (game.beam is the decor beam, not the station's)
findings.fix_correction: Fix 1 works as written: after the last send, current() is undefined, so reading() falls back to JOBS[last] and aim.tx isn't re-aimed, and update(0) redraws the last delivered route. Also set the beam's opacity to full in that call, because drawBeam caches on beamKey.

findings.title: Clicking a mirror on the hall map turns the mirror instead of aiming the tower at it
findings.problem:
With Near IR selected and the mirror standing on mark A, the natural first move is to click on the mirror, meaning 'point the tower here'. But pointer() grabs whatever mirror is within 1.2 m of the cursor (handleNear), so a click on mark A rotates the mirror's board and leaves the tower untouched.
- **Observed:** in my run a click at A changed aim.mirrors.A from −1.05 to −0.42 while aim.tx stayed at the lab-pad heading 2.414. The map showed the tower beam still going straight into the shutter (shot 31).
- **What works:** aiming the tower needs a drag that starts away from every mirror and ends beyond it (shots 32–33).
- **Prompt:** the prompt says only 'Drag · Aim the beam'.
- **Size:** the mirror's 1.2 m grab zone is about 57 px on a 22 m map that is only about 360 px wide on screen. So on the small map, the area around the very target you want to aim at is mostly a 'turn the mirror' zone.

This is the one real puzzle in the room, and its first interaction does the opposite of what the player intends.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/spectrum-play-33-bench-tower-on-mirror.jpg (works only after a drag from near the tower to past A)
src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:212-215 (handleNear: any standing mirror within 1.2 m)
findings.fix: In station.ts pointer(): if the press lands near a standing mirror that the tower's beam does **not** reach yet (`!this.reading().route.spots.includes(s)`), treat it as 'aim the tower at that mirror': `this.drag='tx'; this.aimTo('tx',SPOTS[s])` (it snaps to the board centre). Only when the beam already hits the mirror should a press near it start a mirror turn. Draw the turn handle as a knob on the ring rim (the 1.05 m circle at :302) rather than the whole disc, and change the cursor and prompt to 'Drag · Turn the mirror' only over that knob.
findings.verify: Add a spec: at the desk with band nir and the mirror on A, simulate a real mouse click at the map position of A (use a map→screen helper). Expect snap().station.reading.spots toEqual(['A']) and aim.mirrors.A unchanged. A second drag from A's rim toward the lab pad then turns the mirror.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced this with a real mouse. At the desk with Near IR selected and the mirror on A, I hover-scanned the map for the 'grab' cursor and found it at px 760–792 × 500–532. A click near its centre changed aim.mirrors.A from −1.047 to 0.088, while aim.tx stayed at 2.4135 and the route stayed blocked by metal. The code matches: handleNear returns any parked mirror within 1.2 m (station.ts:212-214), and pointer() sets drag to that mirror (:357). The reviewer overstates the size: the grab zone is about 32–40 px across at 1440×900 (1.2 m at about 15.5 px/m), not 57 px. It still covers the very spot the player wants to aim at. A click exactly on the centre does nothing (aimTo returns false within 0.3 m, :201), which makes it more confusing.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log: click near A {before tx 2.4135, A −1.047; after tx 2.4135, A 0.088; blocked 'metal'}

findings.title: After setting the pod or a mirror down, the prompt offers 'E · Pick up the pod/mirror' while the card says to go to the desk
findings.problem:
The moment the pod lands on the storeroom pad, the card moves to 'Sit at the dispatch desk (E)'. But Pip is still next to the pod, so the pill says 'E · Pick up the pod' (shot 10). The same happens after standing a mirror on mark A: the card says 'Delivery 2: Into the shuttered lab' while the pill says 'E · Pick up the mirror' (shot 28).

Both tell the player to press E. Pressing the key the pill shows undoes the step just completed: update() unparks the pod and clears podPad (station.ts:378-379). That is the 'prompt points at the nearest prop, not the current step' failure. It is especially confusing because the card's own instruction also ends in '(E)'.
evidence: src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:435 (pick-up prompt for any nearest pod or mirror)
findings.fix:
In station.ts prompt(false):
- If the nearest grab is the pod and `this.podPad===this.current()?.pad`, return null, or `{key:'E',text:'Work at the desk'}` when near the desk.
- Likewise, if the nearest is a mirror parked on a mark in the current beam route, return null.
- Keep the pick-up prompt only when the pod sits on a wrong pad or loose.

Optionally also show a small parked tick over the pad for 1 s.
findings.verify: Retake shots 10 and 28. The prompt pill is empty, or points to the desk, and never offers to pick the just-placed item up again. Add a spec expecting the `.prompt-pill` text to not contain 'Pick up' right after podPad==='store'.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced both cases. After setting the pod on the storeroom pad, the card reads 'Sit at the dispatch desk (E)' while the pill reads 'E Pick up the pod' (shot 04). After standing the mirror on A, the pill reads 'E Pick up the mirror' (v1 log). nearest() (game.ts:192) doesn't exclude parked fixed bodies, and prompt() returns a pick-up prompt for the nearest pod or mirror (station.ts:435). Pressing E then unparks the item and clears it (:378-379).
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log 'mirror stood ui': pill 'E Pick up the mirror'

findings.title: The live LINK meter shows the result of every setting before SEND, so Deliveries 1 and 3 are 'press number keys until it goes green'
findings.problem:
The LINK monitor, the hall-map path and the right panel all update live as bands and powers change. A player can therefore solve without predicting anything:
- **Delivery 1:** press 1, read 'CLEAR LINK 11.0 dB', press Enter (shots 12→14).
- **Delivery 3:** press 3, read 'CLEAR LINK 15 dB', press Enter (shot 43).
- **Power:** reading the meter also settles power (1/10/100) with no thought, and that is what the Elegant tier rewards.

There is no risk, no 'aha' and no tension: a failed send can only happen if you ignore a red BLOCKED readout (shot 13). Two of the three deliveries are one key press after a long walk, and the bench tiers reward reading a gauge rather than understanding (brick passes radio, smoke scatters short waves). The physical, world-first cue (the drawn beam stopping at the brick with a red disc) is good; it's the numeric preview that removes the decision.
evidence: src/stations/spectrum/station.ts:443-444 (prompt hands the next key: 'P Power' then 'Enter Send')
findings.fix:
Keep the drawn path on the map and in the room (cause in the world), but:
- Hide the dB number, the bar and 'CLEAR/WEAK' until SEND. Before SEND, show only inputs: band, λ, power, and 'path: reaches the pod / stopped at X'.
- After SEND, reveal the margin bar with an animated fill, and keep a 3-row 'last sends' log on the LINK screen.
- Remove the prompt 'P · Power' (:443), which tells the player to raise power.

To give Deliveries 1 and 3 an act (see the separate walking and detector findings), consider making the pod's detector heads physical props on the desk rack that Pip fits by hand (R4B 'Bounce House').
findings.verify: At the desk with band radio, before SEND, snap the LINK screen: no dB value is shown. After SEND the margin appears. A play-test (or scripted brute force) shows that cycling bands without sending gives no margin readout.
findings.verify_reason: The behaviour is real. drawLink (station.ts:329-341) and the panel (:414-428) show the live margin and CLEAR/WEAK for every band and power before SEND, and no cost is charged until send (:231). In my run, pressing radio immediately gave pill 'Enter Send' and CLEAR LINK. The prompt also steers power ('P · Power' when the margin is under the reliable level, :443). That cuts against DR-38: free cycling through the five bands shows the answer.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log 'after radio ui': pill 'Enter Send' immediately after pressing radio
findings.fix_correction: Hiding the margin and making SEND the only test would push players toward trial sends, and each failed send counts as a mistake and costs energy. That is also trial-and-error under DR-38. Keep the qualitative world cue before SEND ('path reaches the pod / stopped at brick'). Reveal the dB number only after SEND, or after the band has been held for a beat. Don't count a failed send as a mistake when its margin had never been shown. Removing the 'P · Power' prompt is right.

findings.title: No cable anywhere in the room, and the slingshot doesn't exist here
findings.problem: AGENTS 4 makes the cable the star of every room. Spectrum has a level `anchor` and `length:10` (levels/spectrum.ts:32), but station rooms neither simulate nor draw the cable (game.ts:104 and :348 skip simulateCable when a station exists). No cable is visible in any of my shots, and snap().rope stays {length:0, maxLength:10}. There is no drag, route, wrap, plug or slingshot act; the closest stand-in is the drawn beam, which can't be grabbed.
findings.fix:
Give the room one physical lead that matters, without changing the teaching:
- **Option A:** the transmitter tower's power or coax lead is a real reel (anchor at the storeroom side wall, about 10 m). Pip drags it from a floor box to the tower base at the start (step 0 'Power up the tower'). Its strain colours and wrap round the desk are visible, and an overstretch plus Q slingshot can fling the cones and crates by the tea corner.
- **Option B:** the pod is tethered to a long data lead, so carrying it to the quiet room means routing a finite cable round the desk and tower.

Either way, enable the rope in game.ts for this station (a `station.cable?:true` flag) and draw it with the existing rope renderer.
findings.verify: snap().rope.maxLength > 0, and a cable is visible at the game camera in the start shot. A scripted overstretch plus Q moves at least one prop more than 1 m (DR-06).
findings.verify_reason: snap().rope at the start is {length:0, maxLength:10, bends:[], strain:0}. game.ts:104 hides the plug, target, socket and anchor when a station exists, and :106 and :348 skip simulateCable and drawCable for stations. No cable shows in my start shot. RULES DR-05 'Known' already says to file this as P1 fun when a room has neither a bench lead nor a room cable.

findings.title: No chaos route and no chaos bonus; the only physical horseplay (throwing the pod) is punished
findings.problem:
**No chaos goals.** All three bonuses are tidy ones: 'Every delivery reliable', 'Elegant: least power, fewest mirrors', 'No failed send' (station.ts:94-97). Nothing in the room rewards slapstick, and there is no absurd shortcut.

**Thrown pod is ignored.** A pod thrown over the brick wall or onto a pad isn't accepted, because station.dropped() only runs on an E-drop (game.ts interact).

**Chaos is costly.** Throwing the pod once on the open floor marked it damaged: snap went from damage 0, cost 0 to damage 1, cost 30 (shot 51 HUD). The station's own limits are damage 1 and cost ceil(4×1.25)=5 (station.ts:60, :82), so one playful throw blows the cost axis by 6×. Only 'best of three' plus a 540 s time limit hides it.

**What works.** Coworkers do react: a thrown plant next to the tea coworker raised alarmed=2 within 0.2 s (shot 65), and that is good. But nothing invites the player to cause it.
findings.fix:
Add one truthful chaos shortcut and a matching bonus:
- **Smoke shortcut:** knock the smoking toaster off the tea counter (throw a prop at it, or shove the counter). The smoke stops, so SMOKE loss becomes 0 for the rest of the run, and visible or near-IR then work for Delivery 3.
- **Pod lob:** accept a pod that comes to rest within 0.9 m of the current pad after a throw. Hook a check in station.update() for `pod.lastSpeed<.2 && dist(pod,pad)<.9 && !held`, then park it. Bonus: 'Lob the pod onto a pad'.
- **Pod damage:** exempt the pod and mirrors (id'd job items) from prefab damage cost, or cap their cost at 2.
- **Cost axis:** separate breakage from send energy so the 5-credit energy axis isn't dominated by room breakage. For example, limits.cost = energy budget + 60 breakage, or grade energy separately.
findings.verify: New spec 'spectrum chaos': knock the toaster down, then deliver job 3 on visible light to reach won===true. A pod lobbed onto the storeroom pad parks it (podPad==='store'). The bonus list shows a chaos bonus. A run with one thrown pod still grades A on cost.
findings.verify_reason: All three bonuses are tidy ones (station.ts:94-97). Throwing is Q (game.ts:183). It applies an impulse and never calls station.dropped, so a thrown pod is never parked (dropped is only called from the E drop path, game.ts:210). Impact damage (game.ts:335) adds damage++ and the prefab cost (coolbox 30, prefabs.ts:24), which is graded against limits cost 5 and damage 1 (station.ts:60, :82). Reviewer shot 51 shows 1 damage and 30 cost after one throw. This breaks DR-01 and DR-10.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:183 (throw path does not call station.dropped)

findings.title: The grading has no teeth: the time limit is 540 s against a 46 s clean solve, and one thrown prop busts the cost axis
findings.problem:
**Time.** The station limits are {time:540, damage:1, cost:5} (station.ts:60, :82). My clean, bot-speed run finished in 0:46 with all three axes A (shot 45). A human who walks rather than sprints and pauses at the desk should still land well under 3 minutes, so the time axis is effectively always A: a player can dawdle for 9 minutes and still get A. With overall = best of three, every run ends A no matter how messy or slow.

**Cost.** The cost axis mixes the energy units of sends (1–4 each) with prefab breakage costs (coolbox 30, chair 25, crate 5). A single knocked crate already uses the whole 5-credit budget.

The result card shows three A's, so the grade can't tell a careful run from a sloppy one.
findings.fix:
1. Set limits.time to about 3× a human clean run. Measure one with a person; as a starting point use 180 s (bot 46 s × about 2 for walking without sprint × 1.8).
2. Split the cost axis: grade `energy spent` (send cost) against 5, and room breakage against a separate budget (for example 60). Or add breakage to damage only and leave cost as pure energy.
3. Consider not counting the first failed send as damage when the LINK meter was hidden (see the brute-force finding).
findings.verify: A clean spec run grades A on time under 180 s and B at 200 s. A run with one broken crate keeps cost A. tests/station-spectrum.spec.ts gains assertions on grade parts.
findings.verify_reason: My clean run won at 0:43 with time A, damage 0 A and cost 4 A, against limits {time:540, damage:1, cost:ceil(4×1.25)=5} (station.ts:60, :82). Room breakage cost (game.ts:335) and send energy (game.ts:353) are added to the same cost axis, so a single 5-credit crate plus 4 send credits already gives 9, a B. A bigger issue: grade.ts:5 sets overall to [...parts].sort()[0], the best of the three parts, so a time A alone (always true at 540 s) makes the overall A.
findings.fix_correction: Also flag that the best-of-three overall in src/sim/grade.ts:5 is shared by every room. Changing it is a cross-room decision (for example, median or worst-of-three), not just a spectrum limit change. Measure the 180 s figure with a human run before committing to it.

findings.title: Dead walking: almost all of a clean run is carrying the pod through an empty hall, and Delivery 3 is about 30 m of walking for one key press
findings.problem:
Timed on the clean route with the bot sprinting whenever more than 2.5 m from its target (drive.walkTo):
- **Delivery 1:** spawn to pod to storeroom pad 4.4 s; pad to desk 3.6 s.
- **Delivery 2 setup:** fetch the pod back 3.5 s, carry it to the lab 7.3 s, to the mirror stand 3.9 s, mirror to mark A about 3.7 s, to the desk 2.2 s.
- **Delivery 3:** desk to lab, then carry to the quiet room (9.4 s), then back to the desk (about 5.6 s), about 15 s in all.

Total about 43 s of walking in a 46 s run. A human walking at 3.15 m/s (measured) with the pod will take noticeably longer.

The Delivery 2 route visits four places in a zig-zag (back-left, back-right, back-centre, mid-right), and the mirrors start at (−3.4,−5.5)/(−0.9,−5.5), about 6–7 m from mark A (3.56, 0.01). The lab-to-quiet-room carry runs about 11 m down the empty x=10.2 lane past nothing interactive. The centre of the hall between the desk, tower and mark A is a big empty floor (shot 02; ART F18), so there's nothing to knock over on the way.
findings.fix:
- Move mirror2's home next to mark A (about (2.2,−1.4)) and mirror1 near mark B, so the mirror step costs about 2 m.
- Add a pod 'return chute' or a rolling pod cart: after each delivery, the pod rides a short conveyor back to a dock beside the desk, or let Pip push it on a wheeled base at sprint speed.
- Put a mid-route interactable on the long carries: the toaster and smoke shortcut, a coworker blocking the corridor who must be nudged, cones on the x=10.2 lane.
- Fill the empty centre with 2–3 hand-placed clusters clear of the beam lanes (ART F18).
findings.verify: Re-time the clean spec. The longest single walk leg is under 8 s at walk speed, and total walking is under 60% of the clean time.
findings.verify_reason: The geometry is right: mirror2's home (−0.9,−5.5) is about 7.1 m from mark A (3.56,0.01), and Delivery 2 zig-zags store → lab → mirrors → A → desk. But the '43 s of walking in a 46 s run' figure is an artifact of ?manual: drive.act() takes no game time, so desk time is zero by construction, and a human spends real seconds there. The longest leg, desk to the lab pod, is about 23 m, roughly 7.3 s at the 3.15 m/s walk speed. That is under the 8 s line in DR-09 (and under the reviewer's own verify threshold), and the hall has clutter and coworkers along it. Long carries are a real pacing weakness, but this isn't a measured rule breach, so it's P2 rather than P1.
findings.fix_correction: Before moving any mirror home, re-time the spec legs at walk speed with no sprint. Moving mirror2 right next to mark A also makes the mirror-on-mark hint more obvious; that is fine, but put it beside mark A rather than on the beam line.

findings.title: The LINK monitor says 'TOO WEAK' when the beam simply misses the pod, which invites the player to turn the power up
findings.problem: When the aimed beam misses the pod (here the tower is aimed at the mirror, which still faces the tower), read() sets margin −Infinity. The LINK screen's status ladder has no 'missed' case: !podOk, then !detectorOk, then blocked, then m<works gives 'TOO WEAK'. So it prints 'no signal' plus 'TOO WEAK' (shot 33; crop 99), while the right panel correctly says 'Path: misses the pod'. 'Too weak' points a new player at the POWER keys, the wrong fix, and the two readouts contradict each other.
findings.fix: In station.ts:338, insert `r.route.missed?['MISSES THE POD','#ffd66b']` after the blocked case, and make the margin text 'no signal' rather than a dB value. Add the 'missed' state to drawLink's cache key (:330).
findings.verify: Take shot 33 again: the LINK screen says 'MISSES THE POD'. Add a unit or spec check that the link status for snap().station.reading.missed===true isn't 'TOO WEAK'.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it with Near IR, the tower aimed at A, and the mirror still facing the tower. Reading: {margin:null, blocked:null, missed:true, spots:['A']}. The LINK screen reads 'no signal' plus 'TOO WEAK' (crop 21). read() returns −Infinity when missed (logic.ts:244), and the status ladder (station.ts:338) has no 'missed' case. The panel row says 'misses the pod' (:426), so the two readouts contradict each other. The pill also read 'Drag Aim, or another band'.

findings.title: Band, λ and f are printed three times at once, and the bench shows about 62 words outside its monitors
findings.problem:
**Three copies of the band.** Pressing a band key shows the same facts three times:
- the toast 'Radio 100 MHz: λ = 3 m, f = 100 MHz. Every band obeys c = f × λ.';
- the wave monitor 'Radio 100 MHz / λ 3 m / f 100 MHz / c = f × λ = 3×10⁸ m/s';
- the right panel 'Band ● Radio 100 MHz'.

**Two copies of the path and margin.** These show on both the LINK monitor and the right panel ('Path blocked: brick wall', 'Link margin no signal').

**Job title twice.** The job card title 'Delivery 1: Through the brick wall' repeats the panel header 'Through the brick wall'.

**Word count.** The HUD layer at the bench held 62 words (measured via innerText) before any toast, more than double the ~25-word target. That counts the panel ask sentences, seven table rows and the simplified-model disclaimer. It is also above the arcade's known 45.
findings.fix:
1. Drop the band toast (station.ts:222); the wave monitor already shows it, so play only the tone.
2. Remove the Band, Power, Path and Link-margin rows from the HTML panel (:423-427). Keep 'Pod on pad' and 'Lab hatch' only when relevant, because the desk's keys, screens and map show the rest.
3. Move the 'Simplified link model…' disclaimer (:428) to the LINK monitor's footer in small print, or to the pause card.
4. Show the panel ask sentence for 4 s, then collapse it.
findings.verify: Count words in the HUD layer at the desk (`document.querySelector('[data-layer=hud]').innerText`): 25 or fewer. In the bench shot after pressing 1, each value appears once.
findings.verify_reason: I measured the [data-layer=hud] innerText at the bench: 62 words before any toast, 78 after pressing Radio (the band toast), and 94 with the Near IR toast on job 2. Shot 07 shows the band name, λ and f in three places at once (toast, wave monitor, panel 'Band'). The path and margin appear on both LINK and the panel, and the job title appears on both the card and the panel header. This breaks DR-40 and DR-41.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log: bench words 62; after radio 78; nir 94

findings.title: The job card prescribes the method ('stand a mirror on a floor mark') and the hatch is never signposted as a control
findings.problem:
**Method on the card.** Step 4 reads 'Move the pod into the glass lab, and stand a mirror on a floor mark' (station.ts:89). It gives away the Delivery 2 'aha' (bounce the beam off a board) before the player meets the shutter.

**The hatch has no prompt.** The other half of the solution never appears as a prompt. With the beam on the closed shutter, the pill says 'Drag · Aim, or another band' (shot 34). The desk rocker is labelled 'LAB HATCH' with no key, unlike 'POWER (P)', even though H toggles it (:367).

**Hatch on the map.** When shut, the hatch is drawn on the map as plain metal, indistinguishable from the rest of the shutter. Only once open does a yellow outline appear (:295).

**Misleading prompt in job 1.** At Delivery 1 the same 'Aim, or another band' prompt appears for visible light at a brick wall, where aiming can never help (shot 12).
findings.fix:
- Change step 4 to the goal only: 'Get the pod into the glass lab'. Keep the mirror marks and the visible mirror boards as the world's hint.
- Draw the hatch on the map as a small yellow-framed gap even when shut, matching the room's yellow HATCH frame.
- Label the rocker 'LAB HATCH (H)'.
- In prompt(), if the route is blocked by metal at the lab-hatch wall, return {key:'H', text:'Lab hatch'}. If it is blocked by an opaque wall with no way round, return {key:'1–5', text:'Another band'} rather than 'Drag · Aim'.
findings.verify: Take shots 12 and 34 again. The prompt at the brick wall is '1–5 · Another band', and at the closed shutter 'H · Lab hatch'. The card's step 4 text names no tool.
findings.verify_reason: Each part checks out. The step 4 text names the method (station.ts:89). The rocker sign reads 'LAB HATCH' without (H) (:139), although KeyH toggles it (:367). When the hatch is shut, walls() gives the hatch segment mat 'metal' (logic.ts:110), so the map draws it the same as the rest of the shutter, and only the open hatch gets a yellow frame (:295). The prompt at the shut shutter and at the brick with visible light is 'Drag Aim, or another band' (v1/v2 logs). Aiming can't help at the brick, because wood and brick both block visible light (logic.ts LOSS).
extra_evidence: v1.mjs 'bench ui' (job 1 visible light): pill 'Drag Aim, or another band'

findings.title: The pill says 'E · Carry the pod' (and 'Carry the mirror') while E actually drops it
findings.problem: While carrying the pod away from any pad, the prompt shows 'E · Carry the pod' (shots 07, 08); with a mirror it shows 'E · Carry the mirror'. Pressing E drops the item where Pip stands (game.ts interact puts it down). The key does not do what the pill says. A new player who presses E 'to carry' drops the pod mid-hall.
findings.fix: Change the far-from-pad text to {key:'E', text:'Put the pod down'} (and 'Put the mirror down'), or return null and let the marker do the guiding. Keep 'Set the pod on the pad' near a pad.
findings.verify: Carry the pod mid-hall: the pill says 'Put the pod down'. Pressing E drops it (snap().held===undefined).
findings.verify_reason: While carrying the pod mid-hall, the pill reads 'E Carry the pod' (v1 log). game.ts interact() with a held item drops it in place (:206-212). So the key does the opposite of the label, which breaks DR-19. (While carrying a mirror near mark A, the pill correctly said 'Stand the mirror on the mark'.)
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log 'carry mid-hall ui': pill 'E Carry the pod'

findings.title: Phone start and survey: the station panel sits over the middle of the room, and the survey crops the quiet room and the left wall
findings.problem: At 390×844 the 'DELIVERY 1/3 · TO THE STOREROOM / Through the brick wall' station panel sits in the middle of the screen (y≈430–500), just over the floor in front of Pip and the dock (shot 90). In the survey (fixed zoom 44) the room is cropped: the quiet room and the right wall run off the right edge, the left wall is cut, and the panel covers the desk area (shot 91). So 'Tab shows the whole room' fails on a phone.
findings.fix:
- On portrait, pin the station panel under the objective card at the top (as at the bench, ui.css:253), or collapse it to a one-line chip while walking.
- Make the survey zoom fit the room to the aspect: zoom = max(44, (level.width/2)/tan(fov·aspect/2)·1.1).
findings.verify: Take shots 90 and 91 again: the panel doesn't overlap the room's centre, and the survey shows all four walls and the quiet room.
findings.verify_reason: At 390×844 the station panel's rect is y 429–496, x 48–378, right over the floor in front of Pip (shot 30). In the survey, the left (storeroom) wall and the right side are cropped, and the panel covers the desk and the front row (shot 31).
findings.fix_correction: The suggested survey formula is technically wrong. The horizontal FOV is 2·atan(tan(vfov/2)·aspect), not fov·aspect. A fit distance is d = (room half-width·1.1)/tan(hfov/2), with the camera pitch taken into account, then max(44, d).

findings.title: REGRESSION / still open (R3B N4): the transmitter tower's black base and turret arm cut into the right end of the bench view, crowding SEND

findings.title: White clutter crates beside the storeroom pad look like the white RX pod
findings.problem: The clutter palette includes '#e9eef2' (near-white) and '#8fc3e6' (light blue) (levels/spectrum.ts:34). The pod is a white coolbox with a teal lid. In the storeroom a white crate sits right next to the pad (shots 62, 64), and similar pale-blue and white boxes line the front aisle (shot 01). A player coming back to fetch the pod, with the pad half-hidden behind the brick, can mistake a crate for it. Only the prompt text ('Grab the crate' vs 'Pick up the pod') tells them apart.
findings.fix: Remove '#e9eef2' and '#8fc3e6' from the spectrum clutter colours (use kraft '#c98f5a', '#d7a56d' and accents that aren't white or teal). Keep white and teal exclusive to the pod.
findings.verify: In the start and storeroom shots, no prop other than the pod is white with a teal top.
findings.verify_reason: The clutter palette does include '#e9eef2' and '#8fc3e6' (levels/spectrum.ts:34), and pale white and light-blue crates sit near the storeroom pad and the front aisle (reviewer shots 64 and 51). But the pod is visually distinct: a coolbox with a #3bb2c9 lid (prefabs.ts:174), a mast with a detector head, a status lamp and an 'RX POD' tag (station.ts:172-175). The bouncing marker also sits over it. The confusion is possible at the game camera, but I couldn't show a player actually mistaking a crate for it.

findings.title: About 1125 draw calls at the start (1139 in the survey) for an 82-prop room
findings.problem: snap() at the start reported drawCalls 1125 (survey 1139) with 82 props. That is 4–5× the ~250 budget; fps held 60 on the host GPU, but weaker machines will drop to the adaptive-quality path. The live canvas screens, per-label planes (every key plate, pad tag and mark is its own mesh) and per-segment beam meshes add up.
findings.fix:
- Merge the static desk dressing and the label plates into one atlas texture and mesh (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries) as R3B N9 suggested.
- Instance the band and power keys.
- Build the beam as one merged tube per redraw instead of 2 cylinders per leg (station.ts:272-273).
findings.verify: snap().drawCalls ≤ 250 at the start and in the survey.
findings.verify_reason: I measured snap().drawCalls at 1133 at the start and 1130 in the survey, with 82 props and fps 60. DR-24's budget is about 250. The count includes every pass (game.ts:453-454), but other rooms use the same metric (Lunch about 175), so the comparison holds.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs log: start dc 1133, survey dc 1130, props 82, fps 60
findings.fix_correction: The reviewer's attribution to label planes and beam cylinders is unverified. The room clutter (max 220, levels/spectrum.ts:34) and the dressing (room.ts) are as likely a cause. Profile first: count the meshes under SpectrumDesk.root and the beam versus the decorRoot and clutter, or compare drawCalls at the bench with drawCalls in the room. Then merge whichever dominates.

notes.fun:
What works: the room shows its problem before you touch anything. A green beam leaves the tower and dies on the storeroom's brick wall with a red stop disc (shots 01, 08). Radio shows as pink broadcast rings and a dashed line that stops at the lab shutter (shot 17). The quiet room's copper mesh, the smoke and the yellow HATCH frame read as physical obstacles. Delivery 2 is a real, satisfying puzzle: stand the board on A, drag the tower onto it, turn the board through the hatch. A 2° nudge (arrow key) knocks the beam onto the shutter, so aiming matters (shots 33–35). Coworkers react to thrown props (alarmed=2 within 0.2 s, shot 65).
What doesn't work:
- Two of the three deliveries are a single band key-press after long walks. The live LINK meter shows the answer before SEND, so there is no tension.
- About 43 of 46 s of a clean bot run is walking, carrying the pod between corners of a thin, empty hall.
- The success moments are invisible: the beam, the pulse and the pad bursts are hidden at the desk, and the desk flips to the next job instantly. The win shot shows no beam.
- There is no cable, slingshot, chaos route or chaos bonus. The only slapstick available (throwing the pod) costs damage 1 and cost 30 against a 5-credit cost limit.
- Grading is toothless: 540 s time limit, best of three, so every run is A.
notes.playability:
No console or page errors in any of 8 runs. The start audit is clean (overlaps []). The clean route walks without stalls, and drive.walkTo never got stuck.
Forgiving snaps are consistent: the 'Set the pod on the pad' prompt appears exactly where a drop will snap (2.2 m), and the same holds for mirror marks (2.1 m). A dropped, thrown or flat-lying mirror can be picked up again, and parked items unpark cleanly, so I found no soft-lock on desktop.
Problems:
- **Phone (P0):** at 390×844 the bench crops off SEND and the RADIO/MICRO keys, with no touch fallback.
- **Camera:** Pip, the pod and the pads disappear behind the 2.1 m brick and the 2.05 m shutter at the default zoom, because the single occlusion ray clears the wall top.
- **Map aiming:** a click on a mirror turns it instead of aiming the tower at it.
- **Prompts:** 'E Carry the pod' actually drops it, and 'E Pick up the pod/mirror' undoes the step just finished.
- **Draw calls:** about 1125.
- **Timing (bot, sprinting):** job 1 ≈ 8 s walking, job 2 ≈ 20 s, job 3 ≈ 15 s. The longest single carry is about 7–9 s.
notes.clarity:
The scene does most of the explaining: pad rings with floor tags, lettered dashed mirror marks, the HATCH sign, the 'WHAT GETS THROUGH?' wall chart, and the RX pod visibly swapping detector heads. The bouncing marker floats over the pod and then the pads, and stays visible even when the pad is hidden.
Problems:
- **Too much text:** about 62 HUD words at the desk, with band, λ and f printed three times (toast, monitor, panel) and path and margin twice.
- **Wrong status:** the LINK screen says 'TOO WEAK' for a missed beam.
- **Method on the card:** step 4 names the method (mirror).
- **Hatch:** it is never prompted and is drawn as plain metal on the map when shut.
- **Prompt vs card:** the pill contradicts the card twice per run.
- **Small labels:** bench labels are about 10 px and meter captions about 6 px.
- **Lookalike crates:** white clutter crates beside the storeroom pad look like the pod.
- **Marker shape:** the marker is a yellow cone in a room with three orange traffic cones, so its shape is a little ambiguous.
notes.teaching: Not my dimension, but it shapes the fun. The physical ideas are good and truthful at the level taught: brick passes radio, a 30 cm hatch passes light but not a 3 m wave, mesh reflects long waves, smoke scatters short ones. The R4B corrections are in: 20 log d everywhere, near-IR also loses to sunlight, the thermal example is now 'heat cameras', and mirrors are aimed by hand. The live dB preview lets the player pass by reading a gauge instead of predicting. Band hues are still false colour (radio red, near-IR pink) without a caption; that's for the teaching reviewer (DR-35).
notes.models: Out of scope for this pass. Noted in passing: the mirror boards read as glass whiteboards rather than mirrors. The pod's mast and detector head read well when it's carried at zoom 9 (shot 07).

rechecked: R3B N4 (room beam and 'B MIRROR' decal through the bench view): FIXED, both hidden while atBench (station.ts:374; shot 12). Its third part (the tower mast/base cutting into the desk's right end) is STILL OPEN (shot 98), filed as P2.

R3B M7 (spectrum bench labels 6–7 px, GREEN detector label covered): PARTIAL. The detector row is gone, so the occlusion is gone; band and power labels are now about 9–10 px and meter captions about 6 px, still under 14 px (crops 96, 99). Filed P2.
R3B M1 / A12 (phone bench layout): STILL OPEN, and on spectrum it blocks play (SEND and RADIO off-screen, shot 92). Filed P0.
R3B N8 (act() renders one action stale): with real key presses the panel, monitors and map update on the same frame (shots 13, 14). Not seen.
R3B N9 (draw calls): STILL OPEN, 1125 at start and 1139 in the survey. Filed P2.
R4B 'auto-aimed mirrors remove the fun': FIXED, the tower and boards are aimed by dragging on the map and the trace is angle-in = angle-out (shots 33–35). The new click-on-mirror trap is filed P1.
R4B 'three menus (band, detector, power)': FIXED, the detector fits itself to the band (one fewer decision).

R4B truth items (10 log d for LED beams; sunlight swamps only visible; 'body heat' example): FIXED in logic.ts (20 log d for every band, near-IR ambient = 1/3 of visible, thermal example 'heat cameras', shot 44 monitor).
ART F18 (spectrum's thin centre): STILL OPEN, a large empty floor around the tower and marks A and B (shots 02, 20). Folded into the dead-walking finding.

DR-14 forgiving snap: PASS. The pod snaps within min(dist(pod), dist(Pip)−0.6) < 1.6 m and the prompt appears at 2.2 m; mirrors at 1.5 and 2.1 m, consistent with each other (station.ts:190-193, :433-434).
